text:
mira: quick flag from a multilingual bring-up. ran peregrine-multilang-768 on multilang-kb holdout (EN/FR/DE) with float32 and our int8 path. seeing a strange divergence: ONNXRuntime float32 ~= pytorch float32, but Triton float32 deviates a bit and Triton+int8 collapses recall on translated paraphrase pairs. pasting summary + notes.

sam: weird. numbers?

mira: overall R@10 (float_pty / float_ort / float_triton / triton_int8):
```
pt: 0.84
ort-f32: 0.83
triton-f32: 0.78  <-- small drop
triton-int8: 0.51  <-- big drop on paraphrase subset
```

chen: drop only on Triton? that suggests runtime-level graph/EP differences or a tokenization mismatch between client and triton preproc. which tokenizer/version used?

mira: model uses sentencepiece v0.1.95. export path: torch -> torch.jit -> onnx(opset14) -> triton modelstore. client tokenization runs in Python host using sentencepiece v0.1.95 NFKC-normalization true. Triton was configured to run internal python preproc with sentencepiece v0.1.90 and NFKC disabled.

olaf: bingo. non-normalized input could shift token ids and thus embeddings. but that would usually show up in float too. why only Triton+int8 degenerates so badly?

mira: I dug deeper. two issues stacked: 1) tokenizer mismatch (minor input differences) and 2) Triton server applies aggressive graph fusion for Gemm+Add+LayerNorm producing slightly different numerics in fused float32. That small numeric delta is harmless for most pairs but when combined with our per-tensor int8 quant (no static calib and per-tensor weights) it amplified to embedding-norm collapse for near-identical paraphrases in FR/DE.

sam: do you have example failing pairs?

mira: sample paraphrase triplet (EN->FR):
```
q_en: "how to file a complaint?"
q_fr: "comment déposer une plainte ?"

float_dot(pt)=0.92  float_dot(ort)=0.91  triton_f32=0.88  triton_int8=0.14

q_en2: "refund status"
q_de: "R4ckerstattung status"
float_dot(pt)=0.86  triton_int8=0.09
```

chen: yikes. embedding L2 norms?

mira: norms (mean +/- std) on paraphrase subset: pt float 1.02+/-0.06, ort-f32 1.01+/-0.07, triton-f32 0.98+/-0.08, triton-int8 0.12+/-0.09. clearly norm collapse on triton-int8.

olaf: two mitigation hypotheses: 1) fix tokenizer parity (upgrade Triton preproc to same sentencepiece + enable NFKC), 2) change quant export to per-channel weights + static activation calibration with a stratified multilingual sample. Also add a runtime parity checkpoint between ORT and Triton for float32 before allowing quant builds to promote.

sam: can you repro with ONNXRuntime quant path (ORT int8) locally to see if it's Triton-only?

mira: ran ORT-int8 (quantize_static per-channel, 2k calib stratified) -> ort-int8 paraphrase R@10=0.81. So ORT-int8 works when using per-channel static. Problem seems to be Triton int8 path + tokenizer mismatch + our default per-tensor dynamic export.

eval-bot: auto-repro job eq-4470012345-01 executed. quick results: triton with updated tokenizer config (v0.1.95 + NFKC) + per-channel static quant -> triton-int8 R@10=0.80. artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/eq-4470012345/triage.zip

chen: good. action items: 1) enforce tokenizer version + normalization parity between client and any runtime preproc (add config check in model package doc), 2) change default embedding quant export to per-channel + static calib with a multilingual stratified sample (include low-resource lang pairs), 3) add a float32 runtime parity gate: ORT_f32 vs runtime_f32 mean_cos difference < 0.02 on a diagnostic set otherwise fail quant promotion, 4) add a CI rule to refuse per-tensor dynamic quant for multilingual models unless explicit opt-in.

mira: added checklist and opened ticket ML-QLT-5023 with links to artifacts + repro script.

olaf: deploy-bot: pausing peregrine-multilang-768-int8 canary rollout in dedicated Triton pool until parity checks and tokenizer fixes land. ticket RD-2702. @mira please ack when you unpause.

sam: small note for devex: include a tiny "parity probe" harness that sends same bytes to host tokenization and to Triton preproc (if enabled) and compares token ids; fail early if mismatch.

mira: already added a token-id diff dump to eval harness. will push PR for gate + triage script.

eval-bot: summary: root cause = tokenizer mismatch + fused op numeric delta + per-tensor dynamic quant. fix = tokenizer parity + per-channel static quant. Post-fix numbers: float=0.83 triton-int8=0.80. artifacts uploaded.

mira: thanks all. closing once PR merged and canary unpaused. :coffee:
